reconcile.note: Clarke argues the angel had already rolled the stone away, per Matthew, before the women arrived at the tomb, so Luke's report of an already-open tomb is not in conflict.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses that the Synoptics/John show the stone already rolled away when the women arrive, while Matthew alone has them witness the angel roll it back.

quotes.text: According to the latter, as they approach and look towards the grave, they see that the stone has already been rolled away by an unknown hand: whereas the narrative of the first Evangelist has appeared to many to imply that the women themselves beheld the stone rolled away by an angel.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), pt. III, ch. II, on Matthew 28:2 and Luke 24:2.

sides.snippet: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
sides.verseText: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.

sides.snippet: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
sides.verseText: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
